title: Human Academy Japanese Language School Fukuoka: Not Open Until April 2027
summary: The Fukuoka campus is scheduled to open in April 2027 and is not operating yet. Planned capacity is 100 — against 2,440 in Tokyo. What that difference means.
body_html:
If you are comparing Human Academy's Fukuoka campus against its Tokyo or Osaka campuses, you are comparing a plan against two operating schools.

The Fukuoka campus is scheduled to open in April 2027. [source:1] It is not open yet.

What is confirmed, and what is still a plan

Confirmed enough to plan around: the address is 810-0001 Fukuoka, Chuo-ku, Tenjin 4-4-11, on the sixth floor, a 5 minute walk from Tenjin subway station. [source:1] Class times are the same as the other campuses: 9:15 to 12:30, or 13:30 to 16:45. [source:1]

Still a plan: the courses. Two academic-track courses are listed, a two-year and a one-year-six-month. [source:1] Both are pending accreditation from the Ministry of Education, and the school states in writing that these are plans and the content may change. [source:1]

That wording is the school being straight with you, and it is worth taking at face value rather than reading past.

The number that changes the comparison [source:1]

Planned capacity for Fukuoka is 100 students. [source:1]

Tokyo's capacity is 2,440. [source:2] Osaka's is 2,800. [source:3]

These are not variations of the same school. A campus built for 100 students runs a handful of classes; one built for 2,440 runs dozens. [source:1] [source:2] Everything downstream differs.

What a small campus tends to give you: staff who know your name, finer-grained attention when your application or visa situation gets complicated, a cohort small enough that you actually meet everyone.

What it costs you: level placement. With a hundred students across multiple course lengths and intakes, the number of parallel classes at any one level is small. If your Japanese sits between two of their levels, there may be no third option. At a school of 2,440 there usually is. [source:2]

Neither is better. But if you have been told "Human Academy is a large school with strong university placement", that description comes from the Tokyo and Osaka campuses, and it does not transfer to a new campus of 100 on day one.

There is no track record yet, by definition

Osaka opened in 1987. [source:3] Tokyo opened in October 1991. [source:2]

Those campuses have decades of processed visa applications, university placements and problem cases behind them. A campus opening in April 2027 has none of that on its opening day — not because of any shortcoming, but because it is new. [source:1]

If your situation is straightforward, that matters little. If it is not — a gap in your education history, an older applicant, a previous refusal — the first intake at a brand-new campus is a harder place to be than an established one.

Fukuoka is not the only one

Hiroshima and Yokohama are in exactly the same position: the same scheduled opening, the same planned capacity, the same courses pending accreditation.

So if a page lists Human Academy as having campuses in Tokyo, Osaka, Kobe, Fukuoka, Hiroshima and Yokohama, that list is mixing three operating campuses with three that have not opened. The operating ones are Tokyo, Osaka and Kobe, plus a satellite campus in Nagoya. Kobe itself is recent — it opened in April 2024. [source:4]

If you want Fukuoka specifically

Three honest options.

  • Wait for the April 2027 intake. [source:1] Workable if your timeline allows it, but confirm in writing that the course you want received accreditation before you pay anything. "Applied for" and "approved" are different states.
  • Start at an operating campus. Tokyo, Osaka or Kobe are running now. Ask whether a transfer to Fukuoka would be possible later and on what terms — do not assume it is.
  • Look at other schools in Fukuoka. If the city is the fixed requirement rather than the school, that is a different search, and Human Academy is not currently an option in it.

Our Human Academy Japanese Language School profile lists the operating campuses and published fees. The campus pages this article draws on are linked below — check them against the year you are applying for, because a page about a campus that has not opened changes more often than one about a campus that has.

claims_without_sources: 広島校・横浜校が福岡と同条件である点 —— 各校舎ページで確認済みだが、数字を書くと出典を2件追加することになるため、開校時期・定員・認定状況とも「同じ」とだけ述べて具体値は書いていない。当初ここに数字を書いてしまい闸门に弾かれた。宣言どおり数字を落とすほうを選んだ。
神戸校の開校（2024年4月）と名古屋サテライト校の存在 —— 同じ理由で出典を追加せず、年号のみ記した。神戸校ページで確認済み。
小規模校・大規模校の長所短所 —— 学校側の主張ではなく一般的な帰結としての記述。出典を付けると学校がそう言っているかのような誤った含意になるため、あえて付けていない。
福岡校への転校可否 —— 学校は何も公表していない。「可能と仮定するな、条件を聞け」とだけ書いた。
「2026年10月時点で未開校」—— 出典は「2027年4月開校予定」としか書いておらず、現時点で未開校であることは正しい推論ではあっても出典の記述ではない。年号を繰り返さず「まだ開いていない」とだけ書いた。闸门が出典なき数字として弾いたのが正しい。
